column2: On the authority of Ibn ʿAbbās (may Allah be pleased with them both), from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, in what he relates from his Lord, Blessed and Exalted is He, who said:
“Allah has written down the good deeds and the bad deeds, and then He made that clear. Whoever intends a good deed but does not do it, Allah writes it down with Himself as a complete good deed;
and if he intends it and does it, Allah writes it down with Himself as ten good deeds, up to seven hundred times, up to many times more.

And if he intends a bad deed but does not do it, Allah writes it down with Himself as a complete good deed; and if he intends it and does it, Allah writes it down as a single bad deed.” Reported by al-Bukhārī and Muslim in their two Ṣaḥīḥs with these words.

His words, “Allah has written down the good deeds and the bad deeds, and then He made that clear…” to the end: what is meant by the writing may be Allah's, the Mighty and Majestic, decreeing deeds and the recompense for them in this detailed manner;
or it may be the angels' writing of the good and bad deeds by the command of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, as He said:
“He utters no word except that with him is an observer, ready [to record]” [Qāf 50:18]. This is indicated by what has come in the hadith of Abū Hurayrah in the Book of Tawḥīd of Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī:

“If My servant wants to do a bad deed, do not write it against him until he does it; if he does it, write it for him as its like; and if he leaves it for My sake, write it for him as a good deed.” There is no contradiction between the two writings,
for both of them take place.

His words, “Whoever intends a good deed but does not do it, Allah writes it down with Himself as a complete good deed; and if he intends it and does it, Allah writes it down with Himself as ten good deeds, up to seven hundred times, up to many times more”: he stressed that the good deed written when one intends it but does not do it is complete,
lest it be thought deficient,

since it is in intention, not in action. He made clear that the multiplication for doing it is up to tenfold and more than that, which is from the favour of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and His kindness to His servants.

It shows that the recompense is multiplied for the deed, not the recompense for the intention, which is clear. As for the hadith, “The intention of the believer is better than his deed”, it is weak, as the ḥāfiẓ mentioned in al-Fatḥ (4/219); see also al-Silsilah al-Ḍaʿīfah by al-Albānī (2789).

His words, “And if he intends a bad deed but does not do it, Allah writes it down with Himself as a complete good deed; and if he intends it and does it, Allah writes it down as a single bad deed”: the good deed for leaving the sin one intended is described as complete
lest it be thought deficient, and the bad deed done is described as single

lest it be thought increased; this is from the favour and justice of Allah. The reward for leaving the bad deed one intended is earned if one leaves it for the sake of Allah. But if he is eager to do the bad deed, his heart is attached to it,
and he is determined to do it if he were able, he is held to account for that. Ibn Kathīr said in his tafsīr, in explaining the saying of the Exalted in Sūrat al-Anʿām,

“Whoever comes with a good deed will have ten times the like of it, and whoever comes with a bad deed will be recompensed only with its like, and they will not be wronged” [al-Anʿām 6:160]: “Know that one who leaves a bad deed and does not do it is of three kinds. Sometimes he leaves it for Allah's sake; a good deed is written for him for refraining from it for Allah the Exalted,

and this is both a deed and an intention; that is why it has come that a good deed is written for him, as in some wordings of the Ṣaḥīḥ: ‘For he left it on My account’, that is, for My sake. Sometimes he leaves it out of forgetfulness and being distracted from it; this is neither for him nor against him,

because he neither intended good nor did evil. And sometimes he leaves it out of inability or laziness, after striving for its means and engaging in what brings him near to it; this one is in the position of the one who does it,
as has come in the authentic hadith from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: ‘When two Muslims meet with their swords, the killer and the killed are in the Fire.’ They said: ‘O Messenger of Allah,
this is the killer; but what of the one killed?’
He said: ‘He was eager to kill his companion.’”
Affirmation of the writing down of good and bad deeds.
It is from the favour of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, that the reward of good deeds is multiplied.
It is from the justice of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, that bad deeds are not increased.
Allah rewards intending a good deed, if one does not do it, by writing it as a complete good deed.
Whoever intends a bad deed and leaves it for Allah's sake has a complete good deed written for him for leaving it.
Encouragement to do good deeds and a warning against doing bad deeds.
